Kurimanya Kids • FabLab Cuenca
Assignment 02

Computer-Aided Design (CAD): 2D/3D Software Benchmark & File Generation

Systematic evaluation of 2D and 3D design software (vector and raster), execution of practical design exercises across selected tools, visual evidence documentation, and open-source CAD source file delivery.

Institution: Universidad de Cuenca • Academic Program: Industrial Engineering (6th Cycle) • Prototyping Facility: FabLab Cuenca

1. Software Benchmark Table (2D & 3D / Vector & Raster)

Below is the classification table mapping 2D and 3D digital fabrication design software evaluated for the Kurimanya Kids orthosis project according to category, data type, software name, and brief description.

Categoría Tipo Software Breve descripción
2D Raster GIMP Programa de procesamiento de imágenes rasterizadas de código abierto para edición fotográfica, máscaras y textura de prototipos.
2D Raster Krita Programa de pintura digital de código abierto para bocetos a mano alzada e ilustraciones conceptuales biomecánicas.
2D Vector Inkscape Editor profesional de gráficos vectoriales que utilizan el formato SVG, usado para preparación de corte láser y trazado de patrones.
2D Vector AutoCAD Software de diseño asistido por computadora para dibujo 2D paramétrico de alta precisión, acotado y geometría estructural.
2D Vector LibreCAD Aplicación 2D CAD liviana de código abierto para diseño de planos mecánicos y exportación directa en formato DXF.
3D Sólido Paramétrico Autodesk Fusion 360 Plataforma integrada de CAD/CAM/CAE basada en la nube para modelado paramétrico 3D, ensamblajes y piezas anatómicas.
3D Sólido Paramétrico FreeCAD Modelador 3D paramétrico open-source modular enfocado en ingeniería mecánica y diseño de piezas mediante PartDesign.
3D Malla Poligonal Blender Suite libre de creación 3D para modelado de mallas complejas, escultura digital, animación y renderizado fotorrealista.
Simulación Firmware y Circuitos Wokwi / Tinkercad Circuits Simuladores web gratuitos para prototipado virtual de firmware ESP32 / Arduino, montaje en protoboard y validación de sensores FSR.

2. Practical Hands-On Exercises & Visual Evidence

Exercise 1: AutoCAD 2024 (2D Vector Drafting)

Android logo drafting in LOGO.dwg using LINE, CIRCLE, ARC, MIRROR and TRIM.

1. Workspace Setup

2. Limb Profile (Mirror)

3. Head Circle

4. Head Arc & Antennae

5. Trim & Final Logo

Exercise 2: LibreCAD (Open-Source 2D Profiling)

Minimalist CAD engine for direct 2D laser-cutting DXF preparation

LibreCAD was evaluated as a zero-cost, lightweight alternative for FabLab vector workflows. We constructed a mechanical mounting bracket using absolute coordinate inputs, circle tangencies and segment intersections to verify DXF interoperability.

1. Perimeter Layout & Intersections

Orthogonal reference segments and circle centers at exact dimensional coordinates.

2. Modify Tools: Mirror

Tools > Modify menu used to edit and mirror the drawn geometry.

3. Final 2D Contour

Closed bracket outline with a central hole and side notches.

Exercise 3: FreeCAD (Parametric Solid Modeling & PartDesign)

Fully constrained sketches, pads, pockets and edge chamfering

In FreeCAD we focused on the Part Design Workbench. We generated a fully constrained 2D sketch, extruded it into a 3D solid pad, rounded the corners with a fillet and added mounting holes to model a baseplate suitable for additive manufacturing.

1. Sketch & Pad Command

Rectangular sketch in Part Design, ready to be extruded with the Pad tool.

2. Constrained Sketch & Fillet

Rounded-rectangle sketch reported as fully constrained, with the Fillet feature in the model tree.

3. Final Part with Holes

Solid plate with four mounting holes made with the Hole feature.

Exercise 4: Autodesk Fusion 360 (Cloud CAD/CAM & Anatomical Modeling)

Integrated sketches, revolving features, organic sweeps and rendering

Fusion 360 is the primary design suite selected for the Kurimanya Kids orthosis. In this exploratory exercise we practiced sketching with splines and tangent constraints, extruding profiles and cutting relief features to create a circular disc with a hanging tab.

1. Base Sketch & Rectangle

Circle and rectangle with constraints on the top plane.

2. Splines & Tangents

Organic curves traced with control-point splines and tangent constraints.

3. Completed Sketch

Face sketch with eyes and nose inside the circular disc and hanging tab.

4. Extrude Profiles

Selecting the sketch profiles in the Extrude dialog.

5. Extruded Solid Model

Final disc with relief cuts and the hanging tab.

Exercise 5: Blender (Mesh Modeling & Subdivision Surfaces)

Primitive meshes, extrusion and Subdivision Surface modifier

Blender was evaluated for organic polygonal modeling. We practiced working from primitive meshes, editing in Edit Mode, extruding faces along an axis and smoothing the result with a Subdivision Surface modifier.

1. Default Scene

Starting scene in Object Mode with the default cube and its Transform properties.

2. Edit Mode & Subdivision

Catmull-Clark Subdivision Surface smoothing the mesh, and the Add > Mesh primitives menu.

3. Extrude Region

Extruding the top face of the cube along the Z axis.
